note: The main banks were taken as Bosnia and Herzegovina's three largest by assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): UniCredit Bank, Raiffeisen Bank BiH and Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, with Sparkasse Bank BiH kept from the earlier reading. Sparkasse Bank BiH: its standard information sheet for its MasterCard revolving card (published July 2025), read again 2026-10-30. It bears a fixed 13.99% a year and costs 3.50 marks a month and 20 marks to process the application to issue it (none within its SPAR packages, which the game doesn't hold). The monthly minimum is 4% of the principal owed plus all the fees and interest due. A cash withdrawal at the bank's own ATM or POS costs 1.50% plus 10 marks (others' not written). In the Federation, overdue sums bear the statutory default rate, stated as 10.00% a year on the sheet's date; it is set by law, lower than the card's rate and varies, so it isn't written as a penalty. UniCredit's, Raiffeisen's and Intesa's card terms weren't reached in this pass and aren't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026): ASA Banka was added as the next issuer reached that publishes its card terms; UniCredit Bank's site answered 403, NLB Banka's and Addiko Bank's (Sarajevo) reset the connection, and Raiffeisen Bank BiH's rate overview (29 September 2026) and its Mastercard Shopping information sheet (April 2023) print the cards' nominal rate, 13.99%, without saying by what period, so Raiffeisen isn't written. ASA Banka's representative information sheets for the Federation and Brčko District (in force from 27 July 2026), read 30 October 2026, for its Mastercard Standard Revolving and Premium credit cards: each bears a fixed 15.99% a year; the Standard costs 30 marks a year and 4.50 marks a month for the card account, the Premium 50 a year and 10 a month; the monthly payment is at least 5% of the limit used plus the month's interest and fees (the fees not modelled; the Premium's also adds any unpaid amount due); a cash withdrawal at the bank's own ATMs costs 1.5% plus 12 marks (others' 1.5% plus 15, not written); a purchase or withdrawal abroad carries a 1% conversion commission. The promissory notes (10 marks), credit registry report (5) and certification costs at signing aren't written. Its sheets for the Republika Srpska weren't read. Addiko Bank a.d. Banja Luka (in the Republika Srpska) was added as the third: its standard information sheet for the Mastercard 3u1 credit card (dated 1 July 2026) and the card's page, read 30 October 2026: a fixed 13.99% a year; a yearly membership of 40 marks (none in its Gold and Silver packages, which the game doesn't hold); a monthly payment of 5% of the transactions made, at least 10 marks, plus instalments, interest and fees due (fees and instalments not modelled); payment deferred up to 45 days without interest; cash at Addiko's own ATMs 2.50%, at least 10 marks (other banks' at least 15, not written); foreign transactions 1.50%. Late payment bears the statutory default rate (10.95% a year), set by law and below the card's own rate, not written; the instalment fees and promissory note cost aren't written.
